posts.text: The next time you guys crap on the media, remember that almost everything you're learning about this war and this administration is coming from journalists who are routinely threatened by this White House and its minions. (And I don't mean me; I mean the DC reporters who get these stories.)
posts.summary: Defends journalists against White House threats, critiques media skeptics

posts.text: I don’t think this person read the book.
You’re simply trying to jam the book into what you already think. You didn’t understand the book and you don’t understand it now.

Worse, you're off base about "the trappings of success." What Hoffer really worried about was *so much* success that people resorted to fighting over small differences, not big ones.

You owe me tuition if I have to explain more of this.
Since you didn't read Hoffer, I guess I'll read it for you. He was trying to explain "mass movements" like Fascism, and if you didn't get this part, you didn't understand the book:
I mean, I'm being sarcastic here, but come on. This is a problem of decadence and the end of ideology, not some media issue
Yes, a recurring massive problem in the history of mankind was right under our noses but it took some internet journalism to suss it out
Fukuyama said it before me, Hoffer said it before Fukuyama, and Nietzsche said before all of us
I’m not sure it will. Let’s see what the public reaction to this is.
I specifically said “I don’t mean me”
two, at least, but sure, let's argue about that :)
